history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV seq 2142 duplicates the already-written record 2080.json ('chamunda-mataji-temple-mehrangarh-jodhpur', Chamunda Mataji Temple, Jodhpur). Every web source for 'Chamunda Mata Temple Jodhpur' describes the same shrine: the temple at the southern end of Mehrangarh Fort, dedicated to Chamunda Mataji, the Isht Devi (family/patron goddess) of the Rathore rulers. Rao Jodha brought the idol from the old capital Mandore and installed it in the fort in 1460 to protect the new fort and city (legend: a hermit's curse over the hill was countered by installing the goddess). Damaged by lightning in 1857 and rebuilt. The 2008 Navratri stampede ('Mehrangarh tragedy', 200+ deaths) happened here. Coordinates repeat 2080.json's fort-southern-precinct approximation (verify). Keep-or-drop decision needed for the dataset: remove or merge with 2080.

name: Chamunda Mata Temple
town_description: Jodhpur, the Blue City and second city of Rajasthan, was founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha on the edge of the Thar Desert; it is dominated by Mehrangarh Fort and is the historic seat of the Marwar Rathores.

travel.airport: Jodhpur Airport is ~7 km from the city centre (verify).
travel.railway: Jodhpur Junction is ~4 km from the fort (verify).
travel.road: The temple is inside Mehrangarh Fort at its southern end; reach by taxi or auto-rickshaw to the fort entrance, then walk (fort entry ticket covers the temple).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri/Dussehra (Sept-Oct) for the main celebrations, when crowds are heaviest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM per travelsetu; one source says 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM - conflict flagged, verify locally. Aarti twice daily; fort entry ticket required.
